title: Recovery Ceilings Read from the Account's Recent Charging
content:
On an Employee Meal Account the ceiling a single payroll period's recovery is held to is banded on the state the account stands in and on how heavily it has been charged in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked.

**Clause.** Where the account stands restricted and three or more charges have been accrued on it in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, the recovery ceiling is the uplifted share of the deduction ceiling printed against the plan, that share being 160 percent. Where the account stands active and no charge has been accrued on it in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, the recovery ceiling is the eased share of that printed deduction ceiling, that share being 55 percent. Where neither holds, the recovery ceiling is the deduction ceiling printed against the plan.

## The three bands

| Account state | Charges accrued in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked | The recovery ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| Restricted | 3 or more | 160 percent of the deduction ceiling printed against the plan |
| Active | none | 55 percent of that printed deduction ceiling |
| Any other combination | Any | The deduction ceiling printed against the plan |

## Points of judgement

The charge count is taken over the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked and counts charges accrued on the account, not meals rung and not recoveries remitted. Three charges in that month put a restricted account in the uplifted band and two do not. An account that stands restricted with no charge in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked falls in neither of the first two bands, because the eased band is written for an active account; it takes the deduction ceiling printed against its plan. An account that stands active with two charges in the month likewise takes the printed ceiling.

*Hypothetical illustration.* On a plan whose printed deduction ceiling is taken for this illustration as $200.00, a restricted account with 4 charges accrued in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked carries a recovery ceiling of $320.00, while an active account with none carries $110.00.
